record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: What is the correct quantum-field-theoretic description of the sine-Gordon model with a non-integrable boundary, and can techniques from quantum integrability still be adapted to study how integrability breaks down in that setting?

evidence.quote: Finally, at the back of our minds throughout this work was the thought to look at the corresponding quantum field theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the sine-Gordon model on the half-line $x \le 0$ with Lagrangian density
$$\mathcal{L} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_t\phi)^2 - \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x\phi)^2 - \frac{m^2}{\beta^2}\big(1-\cos(\beta\phi)\big),$$
subject at $x=0$ to a non-integrable boundary condition, for instance a Robin-type condition
$$\partial_x\phi(0,t) + k\,\phi(0,t) = 0$$
with generic real parameter $k$, or more generally a boundary potential $V_B(\phi(0,t))$ that does not fall into the integrable Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov family $V_B(\phi)=M\cos\!\big(\tfrac{\beta}{2}(\phi-\phi_0)\big)$.

Provide a precise quantum-field-theoretic formulation of this boundary sine-Gordon model in the non-integrable regime: specify the Hilbert space, the boundary state/boundary action, and a consistent definition of asymptotic particle states and their scattering off the boundary. Determine to what extent techniques developed for quantum boundary integrability—such as the boundary Yang–Baxter (reflection) equation, the boundary bootstrap, form-factor expansions, and the truncated conformal space approach—can be adapted to compute observables (reflection amplitudes, boundary energies, boundary form factors) in this non-integrable setting, and characterize quantitatively how integrability is broken (e.g., production probabilities for inelastic processes, deviations from factorized reflection, decay of boundary bound states).
artifact.status_search_result: Classical and semi-classical analyses of the sine-Gordon model with non-integrable Robin boundary conditions have appeared (e.g., studies of soliton reflection with intricate resonance structure), and the corresponding quantum field theory has been highlighted as an open direction. No complete QFT description of the non-integrable boundary sine-Gordon model, nor a systematic adaptation of integrability techniques to quantify its breaking, appears to be established in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Breaking integrability at the boundary: the sine-Gordon model with Robin boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Boundary scattering in the sine-Gordon model with a non-integrable family of Robin boundary conditions is investigated; intricate resonance structures arise.
status_evidence.claim: The non-integrable Robin boundary sine-Gordon model has been studied classically/semiclassically but a complete quantum description is not given.

status_evidence.title: Sine-Gordon quantum field theory on the half-line with quantum boundary degrees of freedom
status_evidence.snippet: Treats integrable boundary conditions with boundary degrees of freedom in the quantum sine-Gordon model.
status_evidence.claim: Existing QFT results address integrable boundaries; the non-integrable analogue remains an open question.
